möchtest.en: You'd like to, you'd like to.

bloques.titulo: Talk about the future with the present
texto: In German, to talk about plans, the **presente** is enough with a word of time: **Morgen besuche ich meine Eltern** (I visit my parents tomorrow). It doesn't take a future time.
Future words: **morgen** (tomorrow), **heute Abend** (tonight), **am Wochenende**, **nächste Woche** (next week).
Remember: if you start with time, the verb is still second and the subject goes behind.
**Möchtest du kommen?** (would you like to come?) or **Kommst du mit?** (do you come?).
To accept: **Gern!** or **Sehr gern!** (with pleasure!). To reject: **Leider kann ich nicht** (unfortunately I can't).
To stay: **Treffen wir uns um acht?** (are we left at 8: 00?).

frases.en: What are you doing this weekend?
analisis: what do you do (present with future value)

frases.de: Am Samstag besuche ich meine Eltern. Und du?
frases.es: El sábado visito a mis padres. ¿Y tú?
frases.en: I visit my parents on Saturday. And you?
analisis: on Saturday visit (the subject behind the verb)

frases.de: Am Sonntag mache ich eine Party. Möchtest du kommen?
frases.es: El domingo hago una fiesta. ¿Te gustaría venir?
frases.en: I have a party on Sunday. Would you like to come?

frases.de: Sehr gern! Um wie viel Uhr?
Um acht. Thomas und Anna kommen auch.
frases.es: A las ocho. Thomas y Anna también vienen.
frases.en: 8: 00. Thomas and Anna are coming too.

frases.de: Super! Treffen wir uns um halb acht am Bahnhof?
frases.es: ¡Genial! ¿Quedamos a las siete y media en la estación?
frases.en: Great! Should we meet at 7: 30 at the station?

bloques.pregunta: How do you say «I work tomorrow.» in German respecting the syntactic order?

opciones.explicacion: By placing the temporary warning «morgen» in first position, the subject passes after the verb in position 2.
The subject cannot be left between the adverbian and the conjugated verb.
The correct deinence of the first person singular «-e» is missing.

bloques.pregunta: They cordially invite you to a party and wish to confirm your attendance. What do you say?

opciones.explicacion: Educated and usual expression that means «With pleasure!».
It is used to offer something («Here you go.») or respond to a thank you.
Formula used to decline the invitation because it cannot attend.

bloques.pregunta: What does the «morgen» warning mean with initial tiny?

opciones.explicacion: With a tiny one it indicates the day after; the part of the day is substantive with a capital («der Morgen»).
«morgens» or «am Morgen» is used for that part of the day.
It would be expressed with «heute Abend».
«Möchtest du» expresses a courteous invitation of personal desire.

opciones.texto: You have an obligation to come?
opciones.explicacion: The obligation would be expressed with «Musst du kommen?».
The possibility or permission would be asked with «Kannst du kommen?».
The reflexive verb to be quoted is «sich treffen»: «Treffen wir uns...».
The first person singular is a dative title, incompatible with the plural subject «wir».
The title of the subject of 1st person singular.
1st person singular of the present verb sein: «ich bin».
Disinence of 2nd person singular («du»).
3rd person form singular («er / sie / es»).

bloques.frase: Nächste Woche besuche ich meine Freunde.

opciones.texto: Next week I visit my friends.
opciones.explicacion: «Nächste Woche» places the action in the near future with verb in present inverted.

opciones.texto: I'm visiting my friends at school tomorrow.
opciones.explicacion: Tomorrow would be «morgen».

opciones.texto: I visit my friends every weekend.
opciones.explicacion: That would be «jedes Wochenende».
